messages:
Zoe S (support): hi team — acme reports a flurry of 429s even though they're on a Dedicated reserved pool (monthly contract). happening during a cron-driven fanout at 12:05 UTC. attaching logs below and trying to repro. any quick checks?
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): they say peak lasts ~25s, QPS jumps from 150 -> 2.2k, then falls back. we're seeing user-facing errors and retries. not seeing auth failures.
Zoe S (support): thanks. can you confirm which dedicated pool id and region? also are they using streaming responses?
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): pool id rp-az-eu-03, region eu-west-1. streaming: no, single response per call.
Ashwin (eng-dedicated): quick sanity: Dedicated pools have an allocated steady QPS + burst buffer. if burst > buffer you'll hit pool_exhausted and get 429s. rx sample from router: 
```
x-rwl-pool: rp-az-eu-03
x-reserved-qps: 200
x-burst-headroom: 300
x-router-throttle-reason: pool_exhausted
```
Ashwin (eng-dedicated): that header set means steady 200 qps + 300 burst = ~500 sustained before throttling. 2.2k > burst window.
Ravi (oncall): got it. what's their reserved contract? is there a configured "burst capacity" feature enabled (we have both fixed burst and autoscale burst modes)?
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): contract shows reserved 200 qps standard. we didn't opt into burst autoscale.
Zoe S (support): ok, that explains the 429s. to confirm repro, run this local concurrency test (python):
```
# repro script
import requests
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
URL = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
HEADERS = {'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED', 'X-Redwood-Region':'eu-west-1'}
def call():
  return requests.post(URL, json={'prompt':'hi'}, headers=HEADERS)

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=300) as ex:
  list(ex.map(lambda _: call(), range(1000)))
```
Zoe S (support): you should see 429s after the buffer. collect the response headers (x-request-id and x-router-throttle-reason) and forward.
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): running now, initial ramp shows success then 429s within ~8s. sample response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
x-router-throttle-reason: pool_exhausted
Retry-After: 1
```
Ashwin (eng-dedicated): perfect reproduction. two remediation paths:
- short term: advise customer to implement client-side smoothing/backoff + stagger cron fanout (add jitter) so QPS ramp is below burst headroom. use Retry-After header for backoff. :thumbsup:
- medium term: enable Autoscale Burst on their dedicated pool (adds ephemeral capacity for short spikes). requires config change + billing opt-in for burst usage.

Ashwin (eng-dedicated): note on billing: reserved contract covers steady QPS, autoscale bursts are billed as metered overage. we can check their billing consent flag.
Ravi (oncall): for debugging, ask them to capture one full router trace: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health and include x-request-id from failing calls. we'll map to pool throttle logs.
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): we captured: x-request-id req_0a1b2c, attaching logs.
Support Bot: incident created INC-2026-5487 and linked to thread.
Ashwin (eng-dedicated): I pulled the trace: router shows token-bucket deplete -> pool_exhausted at 12:05:07, bucket refill rate 200/s, bucket capacity 300 tokens. burst pattern: 0->2200 qps spike for 12s. that's a violation of configured headroom.
Zoe S (support): next steps for customer: 1) implement smoothing + exponential backoff honoring Retry-After, 2) consider enabling "burst autoscale" if they need occasional >steady spikes, 3) if spikes are regular, consider upgrading reserved QPS via sales.
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): can we temporarily raise their burst buffer while we decide? they need a fast fix.
Ashwin (eng-dedicated): yes — we can grant a temporary bump to burst_headroom to 1200 for 24h as an emergency mitigation. will require ops approval. Ravi, can you approve?
Ravi (oncall): approved for 24h emergency bump. I'll apply change to pool rp-az-eu-03 now and monitor.
Support Bot: action taken: burst_headroom set to 1200 for rp-az-eu-03 (temp 24h). change id chg_9921.
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): after change, re-ran stress test — errors dropped to <0.5% during the spike window. thanks.
Zoe S (support): great. follow-up: schedule a review with customer to discuss long-term: autoscale vs reserved upgrade + alerting (we can add pool-headroom alerts to their console). I'll create a ticket for enablement + sales handoff.
Ashwin (eng-dedicated): also adding a docs blurb: "Dedicated pools: steady QPS + burst headroom. plan for fanouts >10x steady by enabling autoscale or upgrading reserved units."
Ravi (oncall): closing loop: capture post-mitigation telemetry and ping if anything flips back. :white_check_mark:
Customer Rep (AcmePayment): thanks everyone — this was helpful, we'll follow up on autoscale options.
Zoe S (support): closing thread once we confirm no regressions after 24h. thanks all!
